policy: Supplemental contracts are mandatory even if upstream scenarios using incompatible graph models are excluded. Each scenario requires executable evidence before FP-8 closes.

scenarios.contract: Nodes/edges/paths retain database, table, kind and incarnation identity across UNION, DISTINCT, grouping, nested values and snapshots; equal property values do not merge distinct entities.
Returned graph values do not retain transactions, cannot write through stale or foreign references, and serialize to detached tagged JSON.
On explicit typed fixtures, labels/properties/type/nodes/relationships/length return exact values; absent nullable properties are not fabricated graph properties.
Composed MATCH/OPTIONAL MATCH/subqueries enumerate compatible tables/type alternatives with exact multiplicity, absent-property NULL and stable identity.

Named variable paths support both directions, undirected, zero length, cycles and explicit bounds; preserve relationship uniqueness per clause and repeated nodes where permitted; budget exhaustion is explicit, never truncation.

scenarios.query: UNWIND [1,2] AS n CALL (n) { CREATE (:T {id:n}) } RETURN n
setup: CREATE NODE TABLE T(id INT64, PRIMARY KEY(id))

scenarios.query: UNWIND [1,2] AS n CALL (n) { WITH n WHERE n = 2 RETURN n AS selected } RETURN selected
WITH 7 AS n CALL { WITH n RETURN n + 1 AS answer } RETURN answer

scenarios.contract: Explicit imports, missing imports, imported-name shadowing/collisions, nested invocations and zero-row aggregation have validated compile/runtime cardinality contracts.

Late inner write, iterator, final-result or cancellation failure rolls back every invocation of the statement; earlier successfully staged statements survive only after proven rollback; no inner commits.
Read-only calls reject nested writes before effects; independent readers observe only committed changes; competing writes retain OCC conflicts and durability.

date/time/localtime/datetime/localdatetime/duration constructors, fields, conversions, comparisons and arithmetic cover exact pinned cases and independent month-end/leap/DST/negative-duration tests; no silent nanosecond loss.
Every declared temporal column survives rollback/commit/reopen, WAL recovery/verification, supported indexes, history, backup and typed logical transfer; old binaries safely refuse new layouts.
DECIMAL(p,s), 1<=p<=38 and 0<=s<=p: exact precision/scale, explicit rounding/overflow, arithmetic/aggregates/order/hash/casts independent of host decimal context and without DOUBLE conversion.
Typed LIST<T>, string-keyed MAP<T>, ARRAY<T,n> and STRUCT fields cover nullability/nesting/ownership/DDL/update/equality/serialization, depth and size bounds and mutation-proof snapshots.

Support matrix and executable positive/negative transfer tests cover keys/indexes/parameters/results/Arrow/Pandas/Polars/Parquet/CSV/JSONL/SQLite/CLI/history/copy; unsupported combinations refuse before partial effects.
Pure/NumPy codec parity, malformed/truncated payloads, exact tagged JSON, concurrent reader/writer admission and installed old/new-reader upgrade tests preserve WAL/OCC and data.
Explicit read/write modes, permissions, types, determinism/effects and quotas; writing callbacks receive an expiring transaction-only capability, without commit/store-switch/nested-writer authority.
Unit procedures, named YIELD/YIELD *, nesting and entity/new-value signatures execute; every yielded column is validated even when not selected.

Callback/iteration/close/output failures retain primary errors and roll back all graph effects; denied read-only/permission calls never invoke writes; callbacks are not implicitly retried or sandboxed.

Paired installed-wheel regression plus isolated Pulse API and real browser exercise source lifecycle, search/key decisions, KG paging/edges/counts, serialization, settings/schema/recovery; Core remains provider-agnostic.

Execute equivalent bounded scenarios against immutable reference versions, report type/identity/multiplicity/error/effect differences and dialect adaptations, and withhold unverified comparative claims.
